quests.instruction: A company is building a new school. One person keeps track of deadlines, costs, and which teams must finish which jobs. Who is it?
options: Site Security Guard
Project Manager
Delivery Driver
quests.correctAnswer: Project Manager
quests.hint: Think about the person who keeps everything on track.
quests.explanation: Project managers plan the work, watch time and costs, and make sure each team knows what to do and when.
quests.funFact: Project managers often use charts that show which tasks must finish before others can begin.

quests.instruction: A big shop must get five hundred boxes from a warehouse to twenty stores on the right days. Who plans the trucks and routes?
options: Logistics Planner
Delivery Driver
Warehouse Cleaner
quests.correctAnswer: Logistics Planner
quests.hint: Think about the person who decides what goes where, and when.
quests.explanation: Logistics planners organize how goods travel, choosing routes, vehicles, and timings so items arrive when they are needed.
quests.funFact: Planning routes well can save time and fuel because fewer trips are wasted.

quests.instruction: At a large school, someone decides which class uses which room and when, so no two classes are in the same place. What is this job?
options: School Caretaker
School Cook
Timetable Planner
quests.correctAnswer: Timetable Planner
quests.hint: Think about someone who arranges the school day like a puzzle.
quests.explanation: Timetable planners match classes, teachers, and rooms so everyone knows where to be and nothing clashes.
quests.funFact: Timetables often have to fit around teachers, rooms, and breaks all at once, which makes planning tricky.

quests.instruction: A town keeps hundreds of old maps, letters, and photographs and needs them stored so they can be found for years. Who looks after them?
options: Tour Guide
Photographer
Archivist
quests.correctAnswer: Archivist
quests.hint: Think about someone who protects important records from the past.
quests.explanation: Archivists organize and protect records so that people can study them now and in the future.
quests.funFact: Archivists store old paper away from sunlight and damp so it lasts longer.

quests.instruction: A school wants to know which lunch dishes pupils choose most. Who studies the numbers and shows the results in charts?
options: Accountant
Data Analyst
Dietitian
quests.correctAnswer: Data Analyst
quests.hint: Think about someone who finds patterns in numbers.
quests.explanation: Data analysts collect numbers, look for patterns, and show the results clearly, for example in charts.
quests.funFact: A chart can show a pattern in seconds that would take much longer to see in a long list of numbers.

quests.instruction: Before a school trip, which planning step should come first?
options: Decide the goal and the date
Buy souvenirs for the class
Print photos from the trip
quests.correctAnswer: Decide the goal and the date
quests.hint: Think about what must be known before anything else can be arranged.
quests.explanation: Planning starts with the goal and the date, because the other steps depend on them.
quests.funFact: Plans often work backward from a date to decide when each job needs to start.

quests.instruction: A baker has orders due at 8, 10, and 12 o'clock. What helps most?
options: Start with the latest order only
Start with the earliest deadline
Bake without any plan at all
quests.correctAnswer: Start with the earliest deadline
quests.hint: Think about which job has the least time left.
quests.explanation: Working in order of deadlines helps make sure each order is ready on time.
quests.funFact: Deadlines help people decide which task to do first.

quests.instruction: A café owner has 100 coins to spend on supplies this week. What is the best first step?
options: Spend it all in the first shop visited
Buy the most expensive items first
List what is needed and compare prices
quests.correctAnswer: List what is needed and compare prices
quests.hint: Think about getting the most from a limited amount of money.
quests.explanation: A budget is a plan for spending money. Listing needs and comparing prices helps the money stretch further.
quests.funFact: Many small businesses write a weekly budget so they know what they can afford.

quests.instruction: Why do farmers write a planting calendar?
options: Crops need planting at different times
To decorate the barn walls for visitors
Because plants read calendars at night
quests.correctAnswer: Crops need planting at different times
quests.hint: Think about seasons and how crops grow.
quests.explanation: Different crops need different weather and growing time, so a calendar helps farmers plant and harvest at the right moments.
quests.funFact: Some crops, like lettuce, grow quickly, while others, like apples, take many years to grow.

quests.instruction: In a hospital pharmacy, medicines are stored in labeled boxes. Why?
options: So staff can find the right one quickly
So the shelves look more colorful
So the boxes weigh a little bit less
quests.correctAnswer: So staff can find the right one quickly
quests.hint: Think about avoiding mix-ups when time matters.
quests.explanation: Clear labels help staff find the correct medicine quickly and avoid mistakes.
quests.funFact: Medicines often have names that look alike, so clear labels are very important.

quests.instruction: An office worker receives dozens of forms every week. Which approach makes it easy to find one later?
options: Pile them together in one big heap
Name each one and file it clearly
Hand them to random passing visitors
quests.correctAnswer: Name each one and file it clearly
quests.hint: Think about a system that anyone could follow.
quests.explanation: A clear filing system lets people find the right form quickly, even long after it arrived.
quests.funFact: Files can be arranged by name, date, or topic, depending on what people need to find.

quests.instruction: A shop notices it sells many umbrellas in rainy weeks. What should the stock planner do?
options: Remove all umbrellas from the shop
Raise every price by a random amount
Order more before the rainy season
quests.correctAnswer: Order more before the rainy season
quests.hint: Think about getting ready before the busy time.
quests.explanation: Stock planners use past sales and weather to guess what customers will want, so they order enough in advance.
quests.funFact: Shops often check sales records to learn which products sell best in each season.

quests.instruction: A hospital stores patient records on computers. What helps keep them safe and private?
options: Leave records open for everyone to read
Write passwords on notes in the lobby
Use passwords and limited access
quests.correctAnswer: Use passwords and limited access
quests.hint: Think about who really needs to see the information.
quests.explanation: Passwords and limited access make sure only authorized staff can see private information.
quests.funFact: Many workplaces train staff to protect private information as part of their job.

quests.instruction: A carpenter hangs each tool on its own outline on a board. What does this help with?
options: Seeing quickly if a tool is missing
Making each tool a little heavier
Making the tools slowly grow bigger
quests.correctAnswer: Seeing quickly if a tool is missing
quests.hint: Think about what an empty outline shows at a glance.
quests.explanation: A tool outline makes any missing tool obvious immediately, which saves time and prevents lost equipment.
quests.funFact: Some workshops call these outlines shadow boards, because each tool leaves a shadow shape.

quests.instruction: A hairdresser takes appointments in a booking system. What problem does it help avoid?
options: Customers' hair growing back too quickly
Two customers booked at the same time
Scissors becoming blunt after one day
quests.correctAnswer: Two customers booked at the same time
quests.hint: Think about how a calendar can prevent clashes.
quests.explanation: A booking system shows when the hairdresser is busy, so two people are not given the same time.
quests.funFact: Many booking systems send reminders so customers remember their appointments.

quests.instruction: A company wants its written instructions understood in three countries. Who turns the written text into other languages?
options: Interpreter
Translator
Book Editor
quests.correctAnswer: Translator
quests.hint: Think about someone who works with written words, not spoken ones.
quests.explanation: Translators change written text from one language to another. Interpreters do the same for spoken words.
quests.funFact: Good translators try to keep the meaning, not just swap words one by one.

quests.instruction: A company sells a complicated machine and needs clear step-by-step manuals. Who writes them?
options: Fiction Novelist
News Journalist
Technical Writer
quests.correctAnswer: Technical Writer
quests.hint: Think about someone who explains how things work in simple steps.
quests.explanation: Technical writers turn complicated information into clear instructions that users can follow.
quests.funFact: Technical writers often test their instructions by following them step by step.

quests.instruction: A leaflet about a school fair is about to be printed. Who checks it for tiny mistakes in spelling and punctuation?
options: Proofreader
Graphic Designer
Press Operator
quests.correctAnswer: Proofreader
quests.hint: Think about the final check before printing.
quests.explanation: Proofreaders read carefully to catch small errors, such as wrong letters or missing commas, before something is printed.
quests.funFact: Proofreaders often read slowly, sometimes backward, to catch mistakes.

quests.instruction: On a morning radio show, who speaks to listeners, introduces songs, and reads out the news and weather?
options: Radio Presenter
Sound Engineer
News Journalist
quests.correctAnswer: Radio Presenter
quests.hint: Think about the friendly voice that guides listeners through the morning.
quests.explanation: Radio presenters talk to listeners, introduce what is coming up, and keep the show flowing.
quests.funFact: Radio presenters often work with a producer who plans what will be said and played.

quests.instruction: A tour guide wants every visitor to hear and understand. Which habit helps most?
options: Speaking quietly and very quickly
Turning to face away from them
Speaking clearly so all can hear
quests.correctAnswer: Speaking clearly so all can hear
quests.hint: Think about making sure everyone in the group can follow.
quests.explanation: Clear, steady speech and checking that everyone can hear help a message reach the whole group.
quests.funFact: Pausing between ideas gives listeners time to take in what was said.

quests.instruction: Why do airports use pictures as well as words on many signs?
options: So the signs look much more colorful
So speakers of any language understand
So the airport needs far fewer signs
quests.correctAnswer: So speakers of any language understand
quests.hint: Think about travelers from many countries.
quests.explanation: Pictures and symbols can be understood by people who read different languages, which helps travelers find their way.
quests.funFact: Many airport symbols, such as the picture of a suitcase, are used around the world.

quests.instruction: Mia is seventeen and wants to learn how to drive safely. Who teaches her?
options: Bus Mechanic
Taxi Dispatcher
Driving Instructor
quests.correctAnswer: Driving Instructor
quests.hint: Think about someone who teaches people how to drive.
quests.explanation: Driving instructors explain the rules of the road and guide learners as they practice in a safe way.
quests.funFact: Many driving instructors sit in a car with an extra set of controls so they can help if needed.

quests.instruction: A train is delayed. Which announcement is most helpful?
options: The train is 20 minutes late; update at 3:15
Something has happened, everyone please wait
There is a train, maybe, at some time
quests.correctAnswer: The train is 20 minutes late; update at 3:15
quests.hint: Think about what travelers need to know.
quests.explanation: A helpful message gives clear facts, such as how long the delay is and when the next update will be.
quests.funFact: Clear updates help people decide whether to wait or choose another way to travel.

quests.instruction: A new cook is unsure about an order. What helps avoid mistakes?
options: Guess what the note might have meant
Repeat the order back to check it
Ignore the note and carry on
quests.correctAnswer: Repeat the order back to check it
quests.hint: Think about making sure both people understood the same thing.
quests.explanation: Repeating a message back is a simple way to catch misunderstandings before they cause errors.
quests.funFact: Many jobs use read-back checks, from kitchens to air traffic control.

quests.instruction: Which sequence of planning tasks makes sense for a school concert?
options: Perform, rehearse, book the hall, choose a date
Choose a date, book the hall, rehearse, perform
Rehearse, choose a date, perform, book the hall
quests.correctAnswer: Choose a date, book the hall, rehearse, perform
quests.hint: Think about what must be arranged before the performance.
quests.explanation: A concert needs a date and a place first, then practice, and finally the performance.
quests.funFact: Planners often make a timeline that shows which task comes before which.

quests.instruction: A warehouse must send a thousand parcels by Friday. Which resources must be planned?
options: Workers, trucks, and packing materials
Only the roof of the whole warehouse
Just the manager's coffee
quests.correctAnswer: Workers, trucks, and packing materials
quests.hint: Think about people, vehicles, and supplies.
quests.explanation: Big tasks need enough people, vehicles, and supplies, so planners check each of these in advance.
quests.funFact: Planners often prepare extra supplies in case something is used faster than expected.

quests.instruction: Why do many teams write down decisions after a meeting?
options: So the room can be locked up quickly
So the meeting feels much longer
So everyone remembers what was agreed
quests.correctAnswer: So everyone remembers what was agreed
quests.hint: Think about people leaving the room with different memories.
quests.explanation: Written notes help everyone remember what was decided and who will do each task.
quests.funFact: Meeting notes can be shared with people who were not able to attend.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best describes good planning?
options: Starting work at once and leaving the plan for later
Thinking ahead about goals, time, and people
Choosing only the easiest task to do each day
quests.correctAnswer: Thinking ahead about goals, time, and people
quests.hint: Think about what helps a team finish a big job.
quests.explanation: Good planning looks ahead at goals, time, people, and materials, which helps teams avoid problems and finish on time.
quests.funFact: Even short plans, such as a daily list, can make a big difference.

quests.instruction: Which pair of workers is mainly about sharing information with many people?
options: Underwater welder and coal miner
Tower crane operator and deep sea diver
Radio presenter and technical writer
quests.correctAnswer: Radio presenter and technical writer
quests.hint: Think about talking and writing for an audience.
quests.explanation: Radio presenters speak to listeners and technical writers explain things in text, so both share information with many people.
quests.funFact: Sharing information clearly is part of many jobs, not just writing or broadcasting.

quests.instruction: A town festival needs a plan, clear posters, and announcements. Which team fits best?
options: Project manager, designer, radio presenter
Underwater welder, pilot, and coal miner
Football referee, tailor, and sailor
quests.correctAnswer: Project manager, designer, radio presenter
quests.hint: Think about planning, designing, and announcing.
quests.explanation: A project manager plans the festival, a designer makes posters, and a radio presenter spreads the word, so each one helps in a different way.
quests.funFact: Festivals often use posters, radio, and websites together so more people hear about them.
